source_text: 40.1. Idcirco animas misit, ut cum animantia cetera sponte natis alerentur et nulla satione prolatis neque domorum aut vestium tutamina sibi aut velamenta conquirerent, miserabilis istis necessitas adderetur, ut cum impendiis maximis perpetuis que sudoribus domos sibi construerent, membrorum conficerent tegmina, superlectilem variam diurnorum contraherent egestati, inbecillitatis auxilia animalibus mutuarentur a mutis, vim facerent terris, ut non sua sufficerent gramina, sed imperatas extollerent fruges, et cum sanguinem totum in subigenda tellure fudissent, robigine grandine siccitate spem laboris amitterent et ad ultimum vi famis humanis cadaveribus incubarent et ab hominum formis tabifica macie dissociarentur abiunctae? 2. Idcirco animas misit, ut quae secum commorantes possessionis alicuius nullum umquam habuissent amorem, avarissimae hic fierent et in habendi studium inexaturabili pectoris ardescerent adpetitu, effoderent altos montes et viscera ignota terrarum in materias verterent alieni nominis atque usus, penetrarent abditas discrimine cum capitis nationes et translatis mercibus caritatem semper vilitatemque captarent, exercerent avidum atque iniustissimum faenus et miserorum ex sanguine supputandis augerent insomniam milibus, possessionum semper producerent fines et quamvis provincias totas rus facerent unum, pro arbore una, pro sulco forum litibus tererent, cum amicis et fratribus inexpiabiles susciperent simultates?
pass_a_gloss: Idcirco animas misit—so vs other animals' spontaneous food/no houses, humans get miserabilis necessitas of sweat-built homes, forced crops, blight/hail ruin, even famine cannibal thinness? Or so companions of God with no possession-love become avarissimae, mine earth, usury, stretch estates into provinces and sue friends/brothers over a furrow?
pass_b_english: 40.1. Did he therefore send souls so that, while other animals would be fed on things born of themselves and brought forth by no sowing and would not seek for themselves protections of houses or coverings of clothes, a wretched necessity would be added to these: that with greatest expenses and perpetual sweats they should build houses for themselves, make coverings of limbs, gather various furniture for daily need, borrow helps of weakness from mute animals, do violence to the earth so that its own grasses would not suffice but it would raise commanded crops, and when they had poured all their blood in subduing the soil they would lose the hope of labor by blight, hail, drought and at last by force of hunger lie upon human corpses and be parted from human forms, dissociated by wasting thinness? 2. Did he therefore send souls so that those who while dwelling with him had never had any love of some possession would here become most greedy and burn toward the zeal of having with an unsatiable appetite of the breast, dig deep mountains and turn unknown bowels of lands into materials of another's name and use, penetrate hidden nations at risk of life and by transferred wares always chase dearness and cheapness, practice greedy and most unjust usury and from the blood of the wretched increase sleeplessness by thousands to be reckoned, always extend the bounds of possessions and though they make whole provinces one farm, for one tree, for a furrow wear forums with lawsuits, and take up inexpiable quarrels with friends and brothers?

lemmas.sense: did he therefore send souls—for this?

lemmas.lat: cum amicis et fratribus inexpiabiles ... simultates

choices.choose: Reject farm-toil misery as purpose of sent souls
choices.reject: God sent souls into sweat, blight, famine

choices.choose: Reject avarice/usury/land-greed as destiny from God's presence
choices.reject: Souls from God ordained to boundless possession-lust

notes: Image-likeness: reductio against sending souls into agricultural misery and possessive greed.
